messages:
anya: Quick sync — need to lock launch gating for the Optimize Advisor prototype (batching + caching + quant recs, plus eval-triggered alerts). Can we decide 3 acceptance gates today?

mike: yep, got 15. quick list first pass?

jordan: I think we should separate telemetry gates from quality gates. Telemetry = latency/cost; Quality = eval/regression.

carla: +1. also need a tenant-risk gate: flagged customers (enterprise) must be able to opt-out of aggressive quant recs.

priya: Agreed. Proposed gates: 1) Perf (p95 latency), 2) Econ (per-token cost delta), 3) Eval alert precision/recall threshold, 4) Tenant opt-out flow (not blocking GA but required for Dedicated/Private). Thoughts?

anya: Nice. Let's try to make them actionable with numbers. Proposal: Perf p95 <= 250ms for 1k token seq on dedicated hardware baseline; Econ >= 12% median cost reduction for batchable workloads; Eval alerts FP rate <= 6% on held-out prompt set; No manual infra changes required for tenant opt-out.

mike: 250ms p95 seems tight for mixed workloads. Can we do conditional: p95 <= 250ms for short sequences (<512) and p95 <= 400ms for long (>512)? Otherwise teams will push back.

jordan: I support conditional. Also we should measure cold-start vs warmed KV-cache. Add requirement: warmed cache should be used in >70% of relevant traffic during pilot.

priya: For eval alerts, we need a definition: an alert triggers when aggregate quality (ROUGE/embedding-concordance/LLM eval score) drops > X% vs baseline over N requests. Suggest: >5% drop over 1k evals or 24h whichever comes first. FP cap <= 6%.

carla: Real customers care about false negatives too (missed regressions). We should track both. Set FN <= 10% on our labeled regression set.

anya: Good call. Let's capture final acceptance wording I can paste into the roadmap ticket: 

```
Acceptance gates for Optimize Advisor v0.4 (pilot):
- Performance: p95 latency <= 250ms for seq_len <512, p95 <= 400ms for seq_len >=512 (measured on Dedicated pilot hardware, warmed cache conditions where applicable).
- Cache/Batching health: warmed-KV cache hit rate >= 70% on pilot traffic; average batch size >= 4 for applicable routes.
- Economic: median per-token unit cost reduction >= 12% vs baseline serving profile for pilot workloads (no quality regression allowed).
- Quantization safety: quantized model variants must not regress eval-baseline by >3% absolute on core prompt set.
- Eval-triggered alerts: quality drop detection windows: >5% relative drop over 1k evals or 24h. Alert FP rate <= 6% and FN rate <= 10% on labeled regression sets.
- Tenant controls: enterprise tenants must have an opt-out flag for auto-apply quant recs and an audit log entry for every recommendation applied.
- Rollout controls: canary at 5% traffic, auto-rollback on sustained SLO breach >5 minutes, manual gate for GA.
```

mike: that looks solid. add: telemetry retention for pilot = 14 days, and ability to surface trace samples for flagged alerts.

anya: done — add to ticket.

jordan: Ops note: need a fallback route for when recommended quant variant is incompatible with runtime (ABI/kernel mismatch). Proposal: auto-route to nearest compatible variant and flag metric.

priya: Also: evaluation harness needs a seeded replay of 10k prompts from product-telemetry (anonymized) to validate econ numbers before pilot sign-off. Who owns that?

carla: I'll own the replay harness and the tenant opt-out UX checklist.

mike: I'll own the perf validation + rollout automation (canary + rollback).

jordan: I'll own the eval alert tuning and labeled regression set.

anya: Great. Next steps: I will paste acceptance gates into the roadmap ticket and mark owners. Carla, Mike, Jordan — please drop initial artifacts in the ticket by EOD Thu (1912348900). If anyone can't meet that, ping here. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder: scheduled deploy window for pilot cluster is Fri 09:00 UTC.

priya: FYI — flagged two customers wanting early access, we should confirm tenant opt-out flow before onboarding.

carla: noted. will prioritize opt-out checklist.

anya: Thanks all — short, concrete agreement. Closing thread and moving acceptance into the roadmap doc. :rocket:
